clue.text: Quiet approach for a progressive party

parts.note: whist is an old call for silence, like hush
a drive is the approach road up to a house

explanation.surface: Someone quietly sets off for a party that moves from house to house.
explanation.walkthrough: A whist drive is a British social evening of whist where players move from table to table after each round.
explanation.definitionFit: Players progress between tables during the evening's card games, so this social event is literally a progressive party.

clue.text: Make it difficult for one to hold a picnic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to obstruct or impede
second meaning: a lidded wicker basket for carrying food

explanation.surface: Someone is making it hard for another to organise a picnic.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to impede progress, and the noun is a wicker basket packed with food for an outing.

clue.text: Subscribe to a picket — that's a clue!

parts.note: to subscribe is to sign your name at the foot of a document
a picket is a pointed stake or post

explanation.surface: Someone puts their name to a picket line and declares it a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picket' suggests a strike, but here it is a wooden stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer gives travellers an indication of the way, and figuratively any helpful hint can be called one.

clue.text: The law's ignored, a defeat for the post office

definitions.note: read as 'a law that is ignored'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rule still on the books that nobody enforces

definitions.text: a defeat for the post office
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an item of mail that can be neither delivered nor returned

explanation.surface: A complaint that the law is flouted and the postal service has lost a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an unenforced statute and undeliverable mail, an item the postal service has failed to place.

clue.text: What a crooner does to relax tension

indicators.note: to relax something is to loosen it so it can fall into a different shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer croons as a way of easing stress.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner sings in a soft, sustained, chanting style, which is what intoning means.

clue.text: An advantage for a side

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slight superiority over a rival
second meaning: the border or rim of something

explanation.surface: A sports team is given a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the upper hand over rivals is having this, and a boundary or rim of any object is too.

clue.text: Hot or cold-blooded creature always inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: fish are cold-blooded animals
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Is it a warm-blooded or cold-blooded animal? The clue sets hot against cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot or cold' looks like a pair of opposites; only 'Hot' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running a high temperature with a fever feels hot, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Nat suffers dreadfully next to sister

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters are in a bad, disordered way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nat is in a bad way, sitting beside his sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers' is both part of the letters and part of the signal. In British hospitals a Sister is the senior nurse in charge of a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British nursing hierarchy this grade sits immediately below a ward Sister, so it is next in rank.

clue.text: Walk out on the sands

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an arid, sandy wilderness

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stroll along the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk out on the sands' reads as a seaside stroll; it splits into abandoning and an arid waste.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abandon a person; as a noun it is a dry region of sand dunes.

clue.text: Expatriate repels me, I admit

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so the following word is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to grant a point is to admit it

explanation.surface: An expat confesses that they push people away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has left their native country to settle abroad is both an expatriate and an emigrant.

clue.text: On the back of a lever that's shifted

indicators.note: shifted means moved about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something sits on the back of a lever that has been moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' is part of the letters, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Text printed on the reverse side of the page is found by turning it over, on the back.

clue.text: Three characters central to the sequel to "Kidnapped"

indicators.note: central characters are the letters in the middle of the title named next

parts.note: Stevenson's sequel to Kidnapped is Catriona, whose middle four letters are kept

explanation.surface: A literary quiz about three characters in a famous adventure story's follow-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson followed Kidnapped with Catriona; its centre is CA-TRIO-NA. 'Characters' means letters, not people in the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three people or things is a trio, as in a trio of musicians.

clue.text: Edward suffers — at a picnic?

definitions.note: the toys famed for their picnic in the song

parts.note: Teddy is a pet form of Edward
to bear is to endure or suffer

explanation.surface: Poor Edward endures a miserable outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the song The Teddy Bears' Picnic, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's song describes stuffed toy bears gathering in the woods for a picnic, so they are found there.

clue.text: Fiddling income tax re missing thousand — anathema!

indicators.note: fiddling figures means cooking the books, so the letters are tampered with
missing says something is lost from the letters before them

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Tax fraud involving a missing thousand pounds is a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M out of INCOME TAX RE, then rearrange the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a curse or a thing that is utterly detested and loathed.

clue.text: Rickety sheep put in irons

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
irons are fetters, which shackle a prisoner

explanation.surface: A wobbly sheep is clapped in chains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' looks like a container signal, but the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a building or structure that is tumbledown and in danger of collapse.

clue.text: Impulse to tell someone else what to say

definitions.text: to tell someone else what to say
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to speak words for another to write down

explanation.surface: A sudden urge to put words in someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a guiding principle or urge; the verb is speaking aloud for a secretary to record.

clue.text: Bay horse I would race endlessly uphill

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means reading from the bottom up
endlessly says the final letter is cut off the word just before

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
contracted to I'd
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bay horse is being raced up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay horse' reads as a horse's colour; Bay is the definition. Cardigan Bay is the great bay on the west coast of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardigan Bay is the large inlet of the Irish Sea along the Welsh coast, so it is named a Bay.

clue.text: One who breaks a dish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who shatters things
second meaning: an attractive person, informally

explanation.surface: A clumsy diner drops a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'dish' and the answer are British slang for a very attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word literally names someone who smashes things and is also slang for a stunner or good-looking person.

clue.text: The position of an executor?

parts.note: surface reading: the legal standing of someone carrying out a will
setter's reading: one who executes people, and the platform where they stand to do it

explanation.walkthrough: An executor normally administers a dead person's estate; here it is a hangman or headsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Public executions were carried out on a raised wooden platform, which is where the executioner would stand.

clue.text: Peaceful country making a killing

parts.note: peaceful means calm and still
the United States

explanation.surface: A calm nation turns out to be profiting handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a killing' reads as earning a fortune, but the definition is a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A quietus is a release from life, a death blow, as in Hamlet's bare bodkin speech.

clue.text: The under-tens skate back to town

indicators.note: back says the word before is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a skate is a kind of ray, a flat fish
a borough is a town with its own charter

explanation.surface: A junior team of under-tens skates back into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The under-tens' looks like a children's team. A Yarborough is a bridge or whist hand with no card higher than a nine, named after an earl who bet against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Every card in such a hand ranks below ten, so the holder has only under-tens.

clue.text: Architectural feature, an example of which can be seen about in Spain

definitions.text: Architectural feature, an example of which can be seen

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the country's own name for itself, as said in Spain

explanation.surface: A church feature that tourists will find all over Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: This parse is a best guess at an obscure clue: the opening of ESPANA, Spain's own name, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at the east end of a church, a feature of building design.

clue.text: August, when melons develop

indicators.note: to develop is to grow into a new form, so the letters change shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Late summer, the month when melons ripen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' is capitalised to pass for the month; it is the adjective meaning dignified.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, august means grand, dignified and awe-inspiring, which matches grave and stately.

clue.text: Qualified to become a partner, and acceptable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: suitable for marriage, as an attractive bachelor is
second meaning: fit to be chosen or allowed

explanation.surface: A business associate is approved for promotion to partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a desirable single person as a marriage prospect and anything meeting the conditions for selection.

clue.text: Musicians not allowed to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the word is caught by ear, not spelling

parts.note: not allowed means prohibited

explanation.surface: A group of players has been forbidden to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of instrumentalists playing together, such as a brass or rock group, is a band.

clue.text: Assume responsibility and accept deliveries

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to assume control from someone else
second meaning: to receive goods handed across

explanation.surface: A new manager is put in charge of the goods-in bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to step in and assume control and to receive things handed across.

clue.text: Argue about an issue

parts.note: re means concerning
the indefinite article
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel over some matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a subject of debate; here it means children.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to put forward logical points, to discuss and debate persuasively.

clue.text: Offspring providing close harmony outside

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a descant is a melody sung above the main tune
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A family whose children sing in tight harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close harmony' is a singing style, but 'close' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A child, grandchild or later member of a family line is a descendant, an offspring of that ancestor.
